PO205.name: front-view knee-over-knee seated pose
PO205.description: Adult women over 25 years old, complete with opaque sports top, trousers and flat shoes and socks. Front: Sit on a simple chair, cross your right thigh over your left thigh, and stack your right knee on top of your left knee; place your left foot flat on the ground, hang your right calf naturally, and place your hands on your upper knees. Main support: sit bones, seat surface and sole of left foot; action phase: still.
PO205.design_tip: First find out the contact points of the chair surface, ground, soles of feet, knees and palms, and then compare the front and rear occlusion of the left and right legs. The overlap of the knees of the two-legged leg and the ankle-crossing of the four-legged leg are recorded separately; kneeling on one knee retains the difference between one knee touching the ground and the other foot landing. Getting up is a single frame in motion, and the angle of view, center of gravity, and support relationship are adjusted according to character design needs.

MV009.name: crane or boom shot
MV009.description: The camera is raised or lowered as a whole, changing the observation height and spatial level.
MV009.design_tip: This shows a low-to-high camera move, distinct from a simple vertical tilt. Read left to right; static storyboards show key stages only.

MV010.name: whip pan
MV010.description: Quickly pan to another location, connecting the rise and fall with motion blur.
MV010.design_tip: The middle frame is deliberately blurred to indicate the process of rapid steering, not a failure to focus. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

MV011.name: handheld following shot
MV011.description: Follow the characters hand-held, with slight irregular shifts or tilts in the picture.
MV011.design_tip: The three frames only indicate irregular framing, and the true shaking amplitude cannot be restored from static images. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

MV012.name: stabilized following shot
MV012.description: The camera follows the movement of the character, trying to keep the horizontal line, subject position and movement consistent.
MV012.design_tip: Stable shooting does not mean a fixed camera position, nor does it necessarily mean a long lens. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

ZT001.name: zoom in
ZT001.description: Keep the camera position still and gradually tighten the viewing range by changing the focal length.
ZT001.design_tip: The contrast background is magnified together with the subject; it is different from the zoom lens that is close to the camera position. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

ZT002.name: zoom out
ZT002.description: Keep the camera position still and gradually expand the viewing range by changing the focal length.
ZT002.design_tip: Emphasize changes in framing, rather than moving the camera. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

ZT003.name: dolly zoom
ZT003.design_tip: Also called Hitchcockian zoom or vertigo effect; legend is not a precise optical calibration. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.
ZT003.description: Camera movement combines with zooming in the opposite direction, keeping the subject relatively stable in size while changing the perceived background space.

ZT004.name: rack focus
ZT004.description: Shift sharp focus from one distance level to another within the same shot.
ZT004.design_tip: Instead of a static shallow depth of field, focus on the transition of sharp objects from foreground to background. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

ZT005.name: slow motion
ZT005.design_tip: The three frames are just an indication of adjacent action stages and do not represent the actual playback speed or frame rate. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.
ZT005.description: Playback makes the action appear slower, emphasizing its phases and details.

ZT006.name: time-lapse
ZT006.design_tip: The time span in a fixed composition can be very large, as opposed to the slow motion direction. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.
ZT006.description: Interval sampling compresses time to emphasize longer changes such as clouds, moving sunlight and crowds.

ZT007.name: freeze action with a fast shutter
ZT007.description: Use shorter exposures to record fast actions more clearly and highlight key moments.
ZT007.design_tip: This is a photographic freeze of action rather than a video freeze-frame or slow motion. Read left to right; static storyboards show key stages only.

ZT008.name: slow-shutter motion blur
ZT008.design_tip: Contrast extension of dynamic contours; legend does not provide precise shutter parameters. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.
ZT008.description: A longer exposure blurs or trails moving parts while the stationary environment can remain relatively clear.

NS001.name: point-of-view shot
NS001.description: Present objects seen from the character's viewing position, allowing the audience to temporarily share the character's point of view.
NS001.design_tip: The middle frame indicates what the character sees, and the front and rear frames indicate the viewer; the subjective point of view is not a fixed scene. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS002.name: objective observer shot
NS002.description: Observe characters and spaces from outside the character, without directly entering the eyes of a certain character.
NS002.design_tip: The objective viewpoint can be combined with a moving lens, which does not mean a fixed camera position. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS003.name: establishing shot
NS003.description: First explain the location, character positions and spatial relationships to provide environmental background for subsequent close-up shots.
NS003.design_tip: A wider field of view is often used to create a shot, but establishing function and distant view are not synonymous. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS004.name: reaction shot
NS004.description: Focus on the character's expressions and actions in response to events or other people's words.
NS004.design_tip: The illustration goes from calmness to awareness to reaction; close-ups are not required. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS005.name: insert shot
NS005.description: Briefly highlight key details in the main action, such as the hand holding a key or the object being manipulated.
NS005.design_tip: The details still belong to the main action; they are distinguished from the cutaway shots that shift away from the main action. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS006.name: cutaway shot
NS006.description: Temporarily cut to an object outside the main action but related to the narrative, and then return to the original scene.
NS006.design_tip: The legend uses the clock in the environment as supplementary information and does not treat it as part of the main action. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS007.name: empty or environmental cutaway shot
NS007.description: Use the environment or objects as the main subject, and do not let the main characters directly occupy the picture.
NS007.design_tip: There are no characters in the three frames of the illustration to express the environment, pause or atmosphere; an empty frame does not mean establishing a shot. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

NS008.name: two-shot
NS008.description: Accommodate two figures in the same frame and let distance, orientation and movement jointly express the relationship.
NS008.design_tip: The three grids indicate changes in the relationship; it does not require that the two people always be on the same depth of field plane. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE001.name: shot/reverse shot
SE001.description: Alternate between the viewing directions of both communicating parties to establish a dialogue or confrontation relationship.
SE001.design_tip: Always keep the axis on the same side, so that the sight lines of both parties in the picture are facing each other; the rules of the axis do not mean that you cannot intentionally cross the axis. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE002.name: eyeline match
SE002.description: Connect the character's viewing action to the subsequently presented object of sight.
SE002.design_tip: The orientation of the objects being seen should form an understandable spatial relationship with the character's line of sight. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE003.name: cutting on action
SE003.description: Switch the camera position during the action to connect the action phases and maintain the coherence of time and space.
SE003.design_tip: Taking the door opening process as an example, the same action is continued after switching instead of completing the action repeatedly. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE004.name: graphic match cut
SE004.description: Use similarities in shape, location, or composition to connect different shots.
SE004.design_tip: The legend uses a centered circle to echo; graphic similarity does not mean that the two scenes were at the same time or place. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE005.name: cross-cutting
SE005.description: Switching back and forth between events in different locations is often used to indicate that they occur at the same time or are related to each other.
SE005.design_tip: The three grids are organized according to A-B-A; whether they happen at the same time still needs to be explained by the plot and context. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE006.name: jump cut
SE006.description: Eliminating a process from the same continuous footage or approximate camera position creates a perceptible time jump.
SE006.design_tip: The positions or actions of characters in the same environment suddenly change; the three boxes only indicate the omitted process. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE007.name: montage sequence
SE007.description: Combine fragments from multiple times or scenes to condense processes or establish conceptual connections.
SE007.design_tip: The illustration uses preparation, en route, and arrival to summarize a journey, which does not represent continuous shooting second by second. The legend is read from left to right; static storyboards only represent key stages.

SE008.name: long take
SE008.description: Character actions are unfolded in one continuous shooting, without editing switching within the shot.
SE008.design_tip: A long take refers to duration and continuous filming rather than a telephoto lens; the three panels are keyframes from the same shot. Read left to right; static storyboards show key stages only.

MC001.name: clean bordered narrative panel
MC001.description: Use a complete and clear frame to accommodate the characters and environment, and focus the reading on a narrative moment.
MC001.design_tip: The grid and characters maintain clear boundaries; the example is an ordinary narrative grid and does not rely on exaggerated special effects.

MC002.name: borderless open comic panel
MC002.description: Unclose the grid to allow the characters and partial background to transition naturally into blank space.
MC002.design_tip: Borderless means that no closed rectangle is drawn inside the image; the arrangement dividing lines on the outside of the picture page do not belong to the comic grid frame.

MC003.name: character breaking the panel border
MC003.design_tip: Characters can only cross the inner frame of the example they are in, and cannot cross the lattice of other entries.
MC003.description: Part of the figure extends beyond the original panel border, strengthening a sense of approach, stretching or breaking out of the frame.

MC004.name: detail inset within a comic panel
MC004.description: Add a small grid to the main image to zoom in on details such as hands, accessories, or clues.
MC004.design_tip: Small cells point to the same object in the main screen; avoid interpreting this as another set of character alternatives.

MC005.name: screentone-shaded comic panel
MC005.description: The grayscale levels of people, clothing and environment are organized with discernible dot density.
MC005.design_tip: It is understood separately from which country’s comic style the entire work adopts; this item focuses on the distribution of light and dark dots in one grid.

MC006.name: hatched ink comic panel
MC006.design_tip: The lines turn with the face; do not draw the lines as speed lines covering the entire screen.
MC006.description: Parallel and cross-hatching build volume, cast shadows and materials.

MC007.name: solid-black silhouette comic panel
MC007.description: Use large blocks of solid black to outline the characters, relying on outer contours and a small amount of negative shapes to convey movement.
MC007.design_tip: Focus on silhouette recognition without requiring facial detail.

MC008.name: high-contrast chiaroscuro comic panel
MC008.description: Use solid black shadows and bright surfaces to separate the face and environment, forming a strong relationship between light and shadow.
MC008.design_tip: Some facial structures remain readable, distinguishing it from a completely black character silhouette.

MC009.name: floral lyrical comic background
MC009.description: Replace the realistic environment with flowers, petals and soft decorative backgrounds to emphasize the lyrical atmosphere of the characters.
MC009.design_tip: Flowers serve as expressive symbols inside the panel, rather than requiring floral patterns on the character's clothing.

MC010.name: sparkle-highlight comic background
MC010.description: Use starbursts, highlights, and highlight symbols to enhance a character's appearance or admiration.
MC010.design_tip: Highlights are organized around the character and must not obscure facial features; it is a caricature of emphasis rather than a true photographic exposure.

MC011.name: silent negative-space comic panel
MC011.description: Reduce the environment and dialogue, and use white space and character pauses to express silence, distance or hesitation.
MC011.design_tip: The blank space itself is responsible for the rhythm and atmosphere; it does not additionally fill in the dialogue or speed lines.

MC012.name: rectangular narration-caption panel
MC012.description: Supplement the time, place, or narrative voice with a rectangular text box that is separate from the character's dialogue.
MC012.design_tip: The text in the picture is only a typesetting example and will not be automatically exported as the entry name.

MX001.name: radial focus-line emphasis panel
MX001.design_tip: Focus lines emphasize the focal point rather than directly indicating the character's movement direction.
MX001.description: Radiating lines converge toward a focal point, emphasizing a character, object or intense reaction.

MX002.name: parallel speed-line action panel
MX002.description: Use roughly parallel line groups to indicate movement trends, making the subject's movements easier to perceive.
MX002.design_tip: Preserve the outline of the subject and the direction of movement to avoid mistakenly making the speed line into a line shadow.

MX003.name: vertical gloom-line reaction panel
MX003.description: Reinforce feelings of embarrassment, loss or stress with forehead shadows and drooping vertical lines.
MX003.design_tip: This is manga symbolism rather than actual skin texture or a clinical state.

MX004.name: impact-burst freeze panel
MX004.description: Organize explosive points, radiating short lines and deformations near the action contact points to emphasize the landing point of the action.
MX004.design_tip: The illustration shows the palm slapping the table; the explosion points are concentrated at the contact point, not the ordinary concentration line behind the entire figure.

MX005.name: afterimage continuous-action panel
MX005.description: The action phases of the same character are superimposed in the same grid, and the continuation of the action is represented by afterimages.
MX005.design_tip: Multiple silhouettes belong to the same character's time overlap, not multiple people in the same frame or three consecutive frames.

MX006.name: adult chibi reaction panel
MX006.description: Simplify adult characters into small bodies, big heads and simple expressions, highlighting the brisk reaction rhythm.
MX006.design_tip: These are image-proportion and symbolic treatments; examples still depict adult characters.

MX007.name: exaggerated squash-and-stretch reaction panel
MX007.description: The face and posture are deliberately exaggerated and deformed, and the unrealistic outline is used to enhance the instant reaction.
MX007.design_tip: Transformation serves the performance and retains identifying points such as the character's hairstyle and clothing.

MX008.name: floating-icon reaction panel
MX008.description: Supplement character reactions with floating symbols such as question marks, exclamation points, and sweat drops.
MX008.design_tip: Symbols are visual expressions, not body parts or real objects worn.

MX009.name: oval speech-balloon panel
MX009.description: Arrange ordinary dialogue with elliptical bubbles and trailing lines pointing toward the speaker.
MX009.design_tip: The tail line points to the current speaker, and the bubble space cannot suppress key expressions.

MX010.name: jagged shout-balloon panel
MX010.description: Enhance shoutouts, reminders, or high-octane dialogue with sharp, jagged bubble edges.
MX010.design_tip: The bubble shape expresses the intensity of the sound; the example phrase is for display layout only.

MX011.name: cloud thought-balloon panel
MX011.description: Cloud-like outlines and small round bubbles are used to connect the characters, distinguishing the thoughts in the heart from the spoken dialogue.
MX011.design_tip: The small round bubble points to the thinker, and its shape is different from the pointed tail of ordinary dialogue.

MX012.name: integrated sound-effect lettering panel
MX012.description: Use onomatopoeia as pictorial elements with shape, size and direction to echo the touch points of the action.
MX012.design_tip: Onomatopoeic characters are not included in dialogue bubbles, and the relationship between glyphs and actions is the focus of observation.

SB001.name: thumbnail storyboard sketch
SB001.description: Use a few lines to quickly determine the position, scene, and spatial relationship of the subject in the shot.
SB001.design_tip: The low level of finish was left on purpose, observing the composition rather than the details of the garments.

SB002.name: clean-line storyboard drawing
SB002.description: Use clear line drawings to explain character postures, props, environment and main narrative information.
SB002.design_tip: Compared to the final illustration, the focus is on the legibility of the shot information.

SB003.name: tonal storyboard frame
SB003.description: Use limited grayscale to organize primary and secondary light and dark, and confirm the visual focus of characters and scenes in advance.
SB003.design_tip: The grayscale block surface serves the reading focus without pursuing the final material.

SB004.name: color storyboard frame
SB004.description: Add concise colors to the line draft and basic light and shade to illustrate the light and color relationship of a single shot.
SB004.design_tip: Keep the concise information of the storyboard and do not require every part to achieve the final effect.

SB005.name: perspective layout storyboard
SB005.description: Use perspective auxiliary lines and arrangement of front, middle and back scenes to confirm the character’s position in space.
SB005.design_tip: Construction guides are part of the design process; the example is not a precise architectural working drawing.

SB006.name: action key-pose drawing
SB006.description: Pick out a clear action node and illustrate the movement intention with center of gravity, outline and action lines.
SB006.design_tip: Only one key pose is shown; it does not automatically represent complete motion or in-between frames.

SB007.name: two-character acting and staging board
SB007.description: Use character spacing, orientation, line of sight and body movements to illustrate a communicative performance relationship.
SB007.design_tip: The picture only contains the dispatch of the current moment, not a sequence of front and back shots.

SB008.name: clay-render previsualization frame
SB008.description: Use a simple 3D model to preview shots, scenes, spatial levels and character positions.
SB008.design_tip: The simplified gray model is a way of previewing the expression, and the characters and buildings do not have to have final materials.

FK001.name: environment establishing concept keyframe
FK001.description: Use a scene with a clear subject to instantly establish the story space, scale and direction of travel.
FK001.design_tip: The protagonist can be small and still form a readable narrative relationship with the environment.

FK002.name: character-entrance concept keyframe
FK002.description: Arrange the entrance, silhouette, posture and lighting around the moment the character appears.
FK002.design_tip: Emphasize this narrative moment rather than a front-side-back character model sheet.

FK003.name: peak-action concept keyframe
FK003.design_tip: Unlike action breakdowns, this project only presents a condensed narrative moment.
FK003.description: Select the most recognizable instant of an action so that motion, composition and environment jointly express the event.

FK004.name: emotional-turn concept keyframe
FK004.description: Use expressions, hands, objects and light to condense the key moments when the characters' emotions change.
FK004.design_tip: The objects in the picture are situational clues, not props that must be attached to all characters.

FK005.name: lighting-and-mood concept keyframe
FK005.description: Design the mood of a shot around key light, ambient color, and light and dark levels.
FK005.design_tip: The light color is a design indication and can be selected separately from the general camera position, scene type and painting style reference.

FK006.name: single-frame color-script study
FK006.description: Extract the main color, warmth, value, and mood arrangement from a story node in the color script.
FK006.design_tip: A color script usually comprises multiple images; this entry presents just one single-frame color design.

FK007.name: visual-effects concept keyframe
FK007.description: Preset special effects images using scale and lighting relationships between characters, environments and effects.
FK007.design_tip: It is an original special effects concept, not a screenshot of a certain film and television work.

FK008.name: environment paintover concept keyframe
FK008.description: Overpaint structures, lighting fixtures or fixtures onto realistic scenes and explore design changes in the shot.
FK008.design_tip: The illustration uses AI original images to simulate the overpainting process, and does not use the base images taken by the real crew.

MC013.name: narrow horizontal eye-emphasis panel
MC013.description: Use long and narrow horizontal grids to focus on the eyes and line of sight, allowing readers to pay attention to what the characters are observing.
MC013.design_tip: Partial face cropping is intentional within this panel; the entire narrow horizontal panel should remain visible in the entry image.

MC014.name: tall vertical full-body comic panel
MC014.description: Use long and narrow vertical grids to accommodate complete figures, strengthening the vertical outline and standing space.
MC014.design_tip: The top of the character's head and the soles of the shoes are intact within the inner frame; the blank space on both sides of the paper is not part of the content that has been cut off.

MC015.name: slanted trapezoid tension panel
MC015.description: Make one side or the top and bottom of the frame into diagonal lines, and use unstable frames to enhance the tension.
MC015.design_tip: What changes is the shape of the grid; the characters and the ground do not have to rotate into a tilted camera position at the same time.

MC016.name: circular focus comic panel
MC016.description: Isolate an observation object with a circular border to create a gaze, focus, or soft emphasis.
MC016.design_tip: The circle represents only the comic grid and does not automatically represent the telescope or the character's subjective point of view.

MC017.name: white-line-on-black comic panel
MC017.description: Use white lines on the black ground to depict characters and space, forming a light and dark organization that is opposite to the conventional black lines.
MC017.design_tip: The subject is depicted by white lines, rather than the entire figure being painted as a solid black silhouette.

MC018.name: dry-brush broken-ink comic panel
MC018.description: Use dry-brush ink with breaks, rough edges and exposed whites to emphasize roughness or strong emotions.
MC018.design_tip: The ink should have a visibly white texture and retain the readability of faces and movements.

MC019.name: ink-wash grayscale comic panel
MC019.description: Use the shades and diffused edges of ink to shape clothing, environments and soft atmospheres.
MC019.design_tip: Sfumato represents the use of grayscale ink, which can be understood separately from dot matrix dots and line shading.

MC020.name: selective-color accent comic panel
MC020.description: Only a small area of color focus remains in the predominantly black and white frame.
MC020.design_tip: In this example, only the key rope is dyed red, while other characters and environments are kept in black, white and gray.

MC021.name: detailed-background simplified-character panel
MC021.design_tip: Emphasize differing detail levels between character and environment; simplified figures still need clear poses.
MC021.description: The background retains rich linework and spatial information while the figure uses a few contours to blend into the scene.

MC022.name: detailed-character minimal-background panel
MC022.description: Focus on the characters with lines, textures and expressions, and only use a few environmental clues to explain the location.
MC022.design_tip: The distinction is as fine as the full frame; the background should be actively reduced, not the lack of character boundaries.

MC023.name: foreground-occlusion peeking panel
MC023.design_tip: Occlusion comes from a definite foreground object, retaining enough character features for readers to understand the frame.
MC023.description: A nearby door gap, curtain edge or object obscures part of the frame, creating a sense of peeking and spatial depth.

MC024.name: reflection-led emotional comic panel
MC024.description: Using mirror or water reflection as the main expression information, the real figure of the subject only partially appears.
MC024.design_tip: The reflection needs to correspond to the character's position; it is a narrative device on the screen, not another character.

MC025.name: object-trace storytelling panel
MC025.description: Use the objects, temperature or traces of use left behind by the character to convey her presence and departure.
MC025.design_tip: This project intentionally does not draw characters directly, but relies on the relationship between objects to organize a readable narrative moment.

MC026.name: superimposed-memory comic panel
MC026.description: Superimpose the fainter memory image into the current picture, so that the same frame can accommodate the characters' associations and memories.
MC026.design_tip: The light shadow is a subjective memory image, not an afterimage of action or a new continuous frame.

MC027.name: white-halo character separation panel
MC027.description: Leave a narrow white border outside the outline of the character to separate the subject from dense black lines or dots.
MC027.design_tip: The white edge serves for outline recognition and does not mean that the character is glowing or has a real light source.

MC028.name: doorway frame-within-frame comic panel
MC028.description: Use the doors, windows or arcades in the scene to form an inner frame and place the characters in the framed space.
MC028.design_tip: The inner boundary belongs to the real scene architecture and is distinguished from the additional inserted detail cells.

MX013.name: opaque-glasses-glare reaction panel
MX013.description: Temporarily cover your eyes with the reflection of an entire lens to enhance mystery, calm, or comedic pauses.
MX013.design_tip: The reflection is a caricature exaggeration, but the structure of the frame and nose bridge remain clear.

MX014.name: horizontal eye-shadow tension panel
MX014.description: Use horizontal dark bands to suppress the eyebrows and make the expression look gloomy, guarded or difficult to judge.
MX014.design_tip: The dark band is a partial visual emphasis, rather than completely blackening the entire face.

MX015.name: blank-pupil stunned reaction panel
MX015.description: Temporarily omit the pupil and iris, and use a blank eye shape to express disbelief or paused reaction.
MX015.design_tip: These are comedic performance symbols; the character remains conscious and the image does not indicate a medical state.

MX016.name: shadowed-face eyes-only reaction panel
MX016.description: Press most of the face into black shadow, leaving only eye highlights or a small amount of contour to emphasize the atmosphere.
MX016.design_tip: Unlike horizontal shadows that only cover the eyebrows and eyes, this option puts the entire face into a graphic dark side.

MX017.name: comic soul-leaving-body reaction
MX017.description: Draw small soul images next to the characters, exaggerating to show being struck down or exhausted.
MX017.design_tip: The little floating soul is a symbolic comic book symbol, not an actual death scene.

MX018.name: petrified cracked-statue reaction panel
MX018.description: The characters are temporarily painted as stiff stone statues, and stone patterns or slight debris are used to exaggerate the shock.
MX018.design_tip: Cracks represent symbolic petrification only, without skin injury or blood.

MX019.name: melting-soft cartoon reaction panel
MX019.description: The lines of the characters are softened, drooped or slightly melted, and exaggerated to express frustration, heat or weakness.
MX019.design_tip: Shown as cartoon deformation to avoid confusion with actual tissue injury.

MX020.name: spiking-hair startled jump panel
MX020.design_tip: The hair transformation serves the mood and the basic outline of the original hair style can still be seen.
MX020.description: Hair suddenly spreading, a springing body and changing gestures intensify the moment of being startled.

MX021.name: oversized-sweatdrop embarrassment panel
MX021.description: Add an obviously enlarged sweat drop next to the forehead to highlight embarrassment, helplessness or guilt.
MX021.design_tip: A single sweat drop is an emotional symbol, separate from the realistic state of profuse sweating.

MX022.name: cross-shaped anger-mark panel
MX022.description: Draw a cross-shaped vein symbol on the forehead or around the face to strengthen anger and dissatisfaction.
MX022.design_tip: The symbols do not necessarily depict actual blood vessels and do not represent medical vascular changes.

MX023.name: heart-pupil delighted reaction panel
MX023.description: Replace the pupils with hearts and use comic symbols to emphasize affection, appreciation or strong feelings.
MX023.design_tip: Heart-shaped pupils are an exaggerated expression and can be used to see favorite objects or people.

MX024.name: comic huff-of-steam emphasis panel
MX024.description: Use short white breaths near the nose or mouth to emphasize snoring, exertion or dissatisfaction.
MX024.design_tip: This emphasizes emotional action symbols rather than continuous realistic breath in cold weather.

MX025.name: dashed-outline whisper balloon panel
MX025.description: Use dashed lines or lighter bubble borders to represent a muffled whisper.
MX025.design_tip: The example sentences only illustrate the usage of bubbles and are not used as additional content for character setting or export prompt words.

MX026.name: wobbly-outline trembling speech balloon
MX026.description: A slightly wavy bubble border indicates a tremulous, hesitant, or nervous voice.
MX026.design_tip: Distinguished from sharp shoutout bubbles, the wavy silhouette remains soft and irregular.

MX027.name: off-panel speech entering the frame
MX027.design_tip: The direction of the tail needs to be clear; the character in the painting is the listener, not the speaker of the bubble.
MX027.description: The speech-balloon tail points outside the frame, indicating that the speaker is absent from the current panel.

MX028.name: pictorial thought-balloon panel
MX028.description: Put images instead of words in the speech bubble to visually express associations, ideas, or desires.
MX028.design_tip: Images are contained within bubbles, differentiated by symbolic responses floating around the characters.

GX001.name: theme-to-character visual development board
GX001.description: Translate the key words of the story's identity into visible outlines, graphics, colors and props.
GX001.design_tip: Observe how one theme connects collars, tools and emblems; motifs are more than arbitrarily collaged decoration.

GX002.name: character silhouette exploration sheet
GX002.description: First lower the details and compare the large shapes of the coat, hair and equipment with multiple full-body black outlines.
GX002.design_tip: Silhouette differences should come from design structure rather than simply changing one character's pose.

GX003.name: shape-language character variations
GX003.description: Arcs, squares and sharp corners dominate the shapes respectively to compare the changes in temperament produced by the same identity.
GX003.design_tip: Shape language applies to clothing, hair bundles and props at the same time, and does not regard a certain shape as a personality law.

GX004.name: character value-grouping studies
GX004.description: Keep the silhouette the same and compare how the darker and lighter color blocks accentuate the face, torso, or key gear.
GX004.design_tip: First look at the light and dark relationship of the small picture, and then judge the details; it is not a lighting test in different directions.

GX005.name: character costume colorway exploration
GX005.description: Compare the main colors, secondary colors and embellishment colors on the same line drawing and light and dark structure.
GX005.design_tip: Avoid changing style and pose simultaneously so color variations can be compared directly.

GX006.name: facial identity exploration sheet
GX006.description: Use multiple facial structure solutions to refine the recognition and temperament of the same character.
GX006.design_tip: Keep the approximate age, hairstyle, and expression consistent. Compare the brows, eyes, nose, and jaw rather than differences in expression.

GX007.name: hairstyle silhouette iteration sheet
GX007.description: Keep the character's clothing and facial recognition points, and compare the relationship between hairstyle, shape and occlusion.
GX007.design_tip: Demonstrates the iterative process of hairstyle design; specific hairstyles such as ponytails and braids are still being searched in the hair catalog.

GX008.name: character focal-point and detail hierarchy study
GX008.description: Use density of detail, contrast, and a dash of accent color to guide the eye to key identifiers of the character.
GX008.design_tip: The example sets the chest instrument as the focal point, leaving the rest of the garment with a quieter, larger surface.

GA001.name: layered costume breakdown sheet
GA001.description: Draw the inner layer, outerwear and outer equipment separately to illustrate the stacking relationship.
GA001.design_tip: The inner layer remains intact and opaque; the disassembly of layers is not a stripping display.

GA002.name: costume material callout sheet
GA002.description: Use fabric, leather and metal partitions on the same outfit to compare different surface performances.
GA002.design_tip: The local close-up is consistent with the main image; the indicated material is not equal to the PBR parameters or measured material.

GA003.name: costume closure and seam construction study
GA003.description: Enlarge the placket, pockets, buckles and seams to make it clearer how the garment is put on, taken off and opened and closed.
GA003.design_tip: Prioritize the description of the connection function to avoid different fastening methods in the main picture and the enlarged picture.

GA004.name: costume wear and storytelling comparison
GA004.description: Compare the new and old condition of the same outfit, hinting at the character's experience through wear, repairs, and stains.
GA004.design_tip: Wear and tear is concentrated on contact, folding and use locations, rather than uniform stains covering the entire body.

GA005.name: equipment mounting and storage study
GA005.description: Use front view, back view and partial illustration of how the tool is attached to the body or backpack.
GA005.design_tip: Mount points, access space, and character actions are related to each other; images are for functional purposes only.

GA006.name: costume range-of-motion study
GA006.description: Check the interference position of jackets, armor and equipment by standing, squatting and raising your arms.
GA006.design_tip: The same suit of clothing remains structurally consistent in each posture; it still needs to be verified by the model and binding.

GA007.name: in-game character readability study
GA007.description: Check outlines, colorways, and equipment identification points in a screen close to game viewing distance.
GA007.design_tip: Compare the close-up to the actual look after zooming out; don’t assume the concept drawing is an engine screenshot.

GA008.name: 3D blockout assisted character paintover
GA008.description: First use simple blocks to determine the volume and equipment positions, and then use overpainting to refine the details of the shape.
GA008.design_tip: The gray mold on the left corresponds to the design on the right in terms of posture and main body blocks; this diagram is a simulation method and does not come with an editable model.

GO001.name: otome character standing-pose exploration
GO001.description: Compare the same character's personality, focus, and gestures in multiple full-body poses.
GO001.design_tip: Keep the face and clothing, and focus on the pose; the female example can be used in a leading or supporting role.

GO002.name: visual-novel expression variant sheet
GO002.description: Fix the facial angle and sketch, and create different emotional states through differences in eyebrows, eyes and mouth.
GO002.design_tip: Different from the face selection scheme: the facial structure, hairstyle and perspective of the same character remain consistent.

GO003.name: character identity anchors and motif callouts
GO003.description: Juxtapose hair accessories, eye features and iconic accessories to organize identifying points that can be used across vertical paintings.
GO003.design_tip: Emphasize continuity of one person's features rather than adding mandatory rules to every body part.

GO004.name: same-character wardrobe continuity sheet
GO004.description: Design everyday and formal clothing for the same character while maintaining a connection with hairstyle, color scheme or accessories.
GO004.design_tip: You can still recognize the same character after changing costumes; don't paint different faces with different costume schemes.

GO005.name: event CG composition thumbnails
GO005.description: Use a small composition plan to explore character relationships, sight lines, and emotional highlights at plot moments.
GO005.design_tip: Compare the composition and narrative first, then go into detailed coloring; not three consecutive shots.

GO006.name: event CG color rough to polished illustration
GO006.description: Maintaining a dramatic composition, contrast the large light and color sketch with the detailed face, hands and clothing.
GO006.design_tip: The color rough establishes overall atmosphere; refinement preserves the story focus and spatial relationships.

GO007.name: dialogue sprite staging and text-safe-area study
GO007.description: Put the vertical painting into a simplified dialogue scene and check the character position and occlusion of the text area.
GO007.design_tip: The blank area only represents the layout range; it is not a new interactive interface for this website.

GO008.name: animated portrait parts and overlap preparation
GO008.description: Next to the complete vertical painting, the front and rear hair, sleeves and accessories are shown to illustrate the relationship between the parts prepared for dynamic deformation.
GO008.design_tip: The component representation is not equal to the importable PSD or completed binding; there should be an appropriate amount of completion on the occluded edges.

GP001.name: front side back character turnaround
GP001.description: Arrange the front, side, and back using the same stance, proportions, and horizontal standards to explain the overall structure.
GP001.design_tip: The three views emphasize the corresponding relationship, and it is still necessary to check the seams, decorations and left and right directions in the generated diagram.

GP002.name: A-pose character modeling reference
GP002.design_tip: A posture is one of the expressions of handover, and it does not mean that all projects must use the same angle or skeleton.
GP002.description: Keep the arms appropriately separated from the torso, clearly showing underarms, cuffs and silhouette for modeling.

GP003.name: head turnaround and facial consistency sheet
GP003.description: The same figure is juxtaposed from the front, oblique side and pure profile to check the transition of facial features and hairline structure.
GP003.design_tip: Pay attention to the consistency of design handover; common viewing directions can also be viewed separately in the perspective directory.

GP004.name: prop orthographic and handling callouts
GP004.description: Put together the front-side shape, holding method and body scale of the character's props.
GP004.design_tip: The isolated prop and the same object in the hand retain corresponding shapes, without implying real manufacturing dimensions.

GP005.name: armor and garment construction cutaway
GP005.design_tip: The anatomy only focuses on the structure of the object and uses partial representations of non-human bodies; it is not a producible engineering drawing.
GP005.description: Localized cutaways or exploded sections explain how shells, padding and fabric layers overlap.

GP006.name: signature action key-pose design sheet
GP006.description: Use a small number of key poses to organize the character's center of gravity, prop usage, and signature action language.
GP006.design_tip: Shows action-design milestones and cannot replace complete animation, timing or collision testing.

GP007.name: shared-world character lineup study
GP007.description: Place characters of different identities side by side to examine camp commonalities, silhouette differences, and inter-character scale.
GP007.design_tip: Compare the design relationships between characters and don’t mistake height differences for some kind of age standard.

GP008.name: rough line flat color and final concept progression
GP008.description: Juxtapose the draft, clear line, flat color, and refinement stages of the same design and watch as the information is gradually determined.
GP008.design_tip: The composition and style are maintained at each stage. The juxtaposition of stages only illustrates one finishing method and does not stipulate a unique production process.

SNH001.name: kitchen food-preparation scene
SNH001.description: Cabinets, stoves, refrigerators and worktops form a home kitchen, and a woman in an apron is arranging vegetables on the countertop.
SNH001.design_tip: You can clearly see the contact between the person's hands and the countertop and ingredients, and the operating area, stove and rear window are layered.

SNH002.name: bedroom bed-making scene
SNH002.description: The bed, bedside table, wardrobe and morning light window form a bedroom, and a woman in complete home clothes is tidying up the bedding.
SNH002.design_tip: Use bed scale, character action and bedroom circulation together to establish purpose, rather than only a bedside portrait.

SNH003.name: living-room reading scene
SNH003.description: The sofa, coffee table, bookshelf and carpet form a living room. A woman sits on the sofa and reads a book, with a tea cup on the table.
SNH003.design_tip: The relationship between sitting posture and sofa support is used to clarify leisure activities and preserve the space in the front and rear of the living room.

SNH004.name: bathroom morning-routine scene
SNH004.description: A sink, mirror, bathtub and towel rack form a bathroom, and a woman in full pajamas is brushing her teeth in front of the counter.
SNH004.design_tip: Mirror reflection matches the character; hand, toothbrush and washbasin contact is clear, emphasizing the washing space.

SNH005.name: home-study writing scene
SNH005.description: The desk, lamp, bookshelf and workspace by the window constitute the study room, where the woman sits at the desk typing on the keyboard and checking notes.
SNH005.design_tip: Keep keyboard, chair and arm heights reasonable, using the study layout to express quiet focus.

SNH006.name: balcony plant-care scene
SNH006.description: Railings, flower stands, potted plants and city vistas form a balcony, with women holding watering cans to tend to the plants.
SNH006.design_tip: The operational distance between the figures and the flower pots is clear, and the railings and architectural distant views provide spatial hierarchy.

SNH007.name: laundry-room sorting scene
SNH007.description: A washing machine, clothes drying rack, storage cabinet and clothes basket constitute the laundry area. Women put folded towels into the basket.
SNH007.design_tip: Distinguish the levels of cabinets, machines and clothes baskets, and the clothes should actually fall into the hands of the characters.

SNH008.name: entryway departure-preparation scene
SNH008.design_tip: Doors, shoe benches and hooks establish the route for going out, with realistic bag-strap and hand connections.
SNH008.description: A shoe cabinet, dressing mirror, coat hooks and entrance mat form a hallway where a woman, already wearing her coat, takes a crossbody bag from a hook.

SNW001.name: office collaboration scene
SNW001.description: Desks, computers, file cabinets and glass partitions form an office, and female employees hold tablets to discuss with colleagues.
SNW001.design_tip: The characters should be in the real work flow, and the desks, chairs, screens and collaborative postures jointly express the office scene.

SNW002.name: meeting-room presentation scene
SNW002.design_tip: The line of sight of the presenter and the audience is in the same direction as the screen, and the desktop perspective remains continuous.
SNW002.description: A long conference table, chairs, projection screen and whiteboard form a meeting room where a woman explains material beside the screen to several adult colleagues.

SNW003.name: hospital consultation scene
SNW003.design_tip: The position, line of sight and desktop communication relationship between the doctor and the patient are clear, and the device only performs environmental recognition.
SNW003.description: A consultation desk, examination bed and medical cabinet form a hospital clinic where a female doctor in a white coat talks with an adult female patient.

SNW004.name: laboratory observation scene
SNW004.description: The experimental bench, microscope, closed sample box and cabinet constitute the research room, and a female researcher wearing a laboratory coat observes the samples.
SNW004.design_tip: Keep the height of the table, the contact relationship between the microscope and the posture of the characters, and do not pile props into a useless background.

SNW005.name: secondary-school classroom teaching scene
SNW005.design_tip: The directions of teachers, podiums and student seats are clear, and the movements of characters serve the teaching space.
SNW005.description: A blackboard, projection screen, desks and teaching platform form a secondary-school classroom where an adult female teacher teaches uniformed junior- and senior-high students seated at their desks.

SNW006.name: library reading scene
SNW006.design_tip: The perspective of characters, desktops and bookshelves together form a quiet public reading space.
SNW006.description: Tall shelves, reading tables and large windows form a library where a woman browses a book at a table, with other adult readers between the shelves.

SNW007.name: metro-station commuting scene
SNW007.description: Platforms, gates, waiting lines and trains form a subway space, and female commuters wait in a safe area with their bags.
SNW007.design_tip: Doors, platforms and people share a consistent scale, with standing poses and luggage positions leaving a public passage clear.

SNW008.name: fire-station readiness scene
SNW008.design_tip: It reflects the scale relationship between characters, equipment cabinets and vehicles, and presents the preparation rather than the disaster scene.
SNW008.description: A garage, fire engine, equipment cabinets and bench form a fire station where a female firefighter checks her helmet and coat beside the vehicle.

SNC001.name: hotel-lobby reception scene
SNC001.description: The front desk, rest seats, luggage and elevator entrance constitute the hotel lobby, where a female receptionist greets adult travelers.
SNC001.design_tip: The standing positions and baggage scales inside and outside the front desk should be clear, and reception actions should be consistent with the use of the space.

SNC002.name: hotel-room arrival scene
SNC002.description: Neat beds, luggage racks, tables, chairs and city windows form a hotel room, and a female traveler in casual clothes opens her suitcase.
SNC002.design_tip: Use luggage racks, standardized furniture and check-in actions to differentiate hotel rooms from home bedrooms.

SNC003.name: restaurant table-service scene
SNC003.design_tip: The tray, arms and dining table are in reliable contact, leaving service channels and guest seating levels.
SNC003.description: Tables, chairs, lighting and a preparation area form a restaurant where a waitress sets a plate beside a table.

SNC004.name: cafe barista-at-counter scene
SNC004.description: A coffee machine, bar counter, cup holder and window seat constitute a cafe, and a female barista prepares drinks at the bar counter.
SNC004.design_tip: Characters, cups and coffee machines form an operational relationship, while the background seats and window light illustrate the store space.

SNC005.name: bakery bread-display scene
SNC005.design_tip: The baking pan must have clear holding points, and the product display and the oven area in the back area must be distinguishable.
SNC005.description: Bread displays, a glass cabinet and an oven form a bakery where a female baker places a baking tray in the display area.

SNC006.name: supermarket grocery-shopping scene
SNC006.design_tip: Characters and shopping baskets maintain a real connection, and shelf heights and aisle widths are readable.
SNC006.description: Shelves, shopping baskets, a produce section and aisles form a supermarket where a woman examines products beside a shelf.

SNC007.name: clothing-boutique display scene
SNC007.design_tip: The mannequin and the clerk should be two independent subjects, and the relationship between clothing hanging and hand operation should be clear.
SNC007.description: Clothing racks, fitting rooms, mannequin platforms and a checkout area form a shop where a female assistant arranges a coat on a mannequin.

SNC008.name: hair-salon styling scene
SNC008.design_tip: Mirror reflection, seated client and stylist position are consistent, without floating tools.
SNC008.description: Mirrors, styling chairs, tool carts and a washing area form a salon where a female stylist combs an adult customer's hair.

SNR001.name: beach-walking scene
SNR001.description: Waves, sand, parasols and a plank road in the distance form a beach, and women in light summer clothes stroll along the coast.
SNR001.design_tip: The characters' footsteps come into contact with the wet sand, and the curves of the coast and the horizon provide spatial scale.

SNR002.name: amusement-park outing scene
SNR002.description: The Ferris wheel, carousel, ticket booth and walking trails form an amusement park, and adult women visit with maps and drinks in hand.
SNR002.design_tip: Characters should not be overwhelmed by huge rides, and both foreground activities and rear facilities are identifiable.

SNR003.name: campsite gear-preparation scene
SNR003.description: Tents, folding chairs, camp tables and woodland form a campsite, and women put their equipment on the camp table.
SNR003.design_tip: The tents, tables and chairs are of the same scale as the characters, and the activities of organizing equipment are used to illustrate the purpose of camping.

SNR004.name: urban-park jogging scene
SNR004.design_tip: Clear footfall positions and path direction preserve the spatial relationship between the exerciser and park facilities.
SNR004.description: A greenway, lawn, lakeshore and park benches form an urban park where a woman jogs along the path.

SNR005.name: hot-spring-inn corridor scene
SNR005.description: Wooden cloisters, courtyards, paper lanterns and bathhouse entrances form a hot spring hotel. Women wearing full yukata pass by carrying towel baskets.
SNR005.design_tip: The cloisters and courtyards are used to express the hotel atmosphere, and the characters remain fully dressed and integrated into the walking lines.

SNR006.name: mountain-trail hiking scene
SNR006.description: Mountain trails, rocks, vegetation and distant mountains form a hiking environment, and the backpacking woman walks along the trail.
SNR006.design_tip: The characters and backpack maintain a reasonable center of gravity, and the rocks in the close-up, the mountain trails in the middle-ground, and the mountains in the distance are layered.

SNR007.name: ski-resort preparation scene
SNR007.design_tip: Clear support relationships among ski equipment, hands and snow establish the pre-departure environment and character.
SNR007.description: Ski runs, lifts, equipment racks and a mountain service station form a ski resort where a woman arranges her gear beside a gentle slope.

SNR008.name: airport departure-lounge scene
SNR008.description: The boarding gate, waiting chairs, floor-to-ceiling windows and the aircraft in the distance constitute the airport. The female passenger is holding her suitcase to check the boarding information.
SNR008.design_tip: Luggage, people and waiting seats share a consistent scale; terminal structures and aircraft outside identify the setting.

SNE001.name: gym workout scene
SNE001.design_tip: The layout of the equipment and the complete posture of the characters illustrate the training space, and the reflections in the mirror remain reasonable.
SNE001.description: Exercise machines, mats, a mirrored wall and storage form a gym where a woman does a light warm-up beside the equipment.

SNE002.name: indoor-pool poolside scene
SNE002.description: The swimming lane, water surface, pool ladder and spectator seats form an indoor swimming pool, and adult women are preparing to enter the water by the pool.
SNE002.design_tip: The characters maintain a clear distance from the edge of the pool, and the swimming lanes and architectural structures jointly define the scene.

SNE003.name: dance-studio rehearsal scene
SNE003.description: Barre, mirrors, wooden floors and speakers form a rehearsal room, where women practice dance next to the barre.
SNE003.design_tip: The characters, poles and ground are clearly supported, the mirror images are consistent, and the movements serve scene recognition.

SNE004.name: concert-backstage preparation scene
SNE004.description: Makeup mirrors, clothing racks, speakers and stage passages form the backstage, and the female singer arranges her coat to prepare for the appearance.
SNE004.design_tip: Mirror preparations connect with the stage entrance, using environmental props to distinguish backstage from an ordinary bedroom.

SNE005.name: theatre-stage performance scene
SNE005.description: The curtain, stage scenery, footlights and auditorium constitute the theater, and the actress performs in front of the scenery.
SNE005.design_tip: Performer, stage floor and scenery share a consistent scale, with lighting guiding attention to movement.

SNE006.name: athletics-stadium preparation scene
SNE006.design_tip: The proportions of characters, track and stands are reasonable, and the purpose of the scene is expressed through pre-game activities.
SNE006.description: A track, stands, starting area and scoring facilities form a stadium where a female athlete adjusts her running shoes beside the track.

SNE007.name: night-market stall scene
SNE007.description: Stalls, food cabinets, string lights and pedestrian traffic constitute a night market, with female stall owners handing out lunch boxes in front of the stalls.
SNE007.design_tip: The interaction between stall owners and customers is clear, and the lively level is established with the stalls in the foreground and the lighting in the background.

SNE008.name: wedding-venue greeting scene
SNE008.design_tip: The figure in the dress, the flower door, and the guests constitute the ceremony space, so as to avoid just a vertical painting of the wedding dress without background.
SNE008.description: A floral arch, seating, ceremony platform and decorative lights form a wedding venue where an adult bride greets guests at the entrance.

SNF001.name: Chinese-inspired courtyard scene
SNF001.description: Corridors, courtyards, ponds, stones and flowers and trees form an ancient style house. Women wearing long clothes inspired by Hanfu stop in the cloister and enjoy the scenery.
SNF001.design_tip: Observe the scale of clothing, people and courtyards; the image is an original historical inspiration rather than an archaeological reconstruction.

SNF002.name: palace-hall audience scene
SNF002.design_tip: The characters are connected with the height difference of the palace and the perspective of the columns, reflecting the depth of the ceremonial space.
SNF002.description: Tall columns, screens, steps and ceremonial furnishings form a palace hall where an adult female steward unrolls a document.

SNF003.name: Chinese-opera backstage scene
SNF003.description: The dressing table, costume rack, headdress box and curtain form the backstage of the opera, where adult actresses adjust their hairdresses in front of the mirror.
SNF003.design_tip: The headgear, characters and dressing table have real contact; the backstage working status distinguishes the formal stage performance.

SNF004.name: Republican-era-inspired street scene
SNF004.description: Old-style storefronts, tram tracks, arcades and street lamps constitute modern urban streets. Women in long coats pass by holding umbrellas.
SNF004.design_tip: Clear street perspective and pedestrian scale; clothing and buildings combine period-film inspirations.

SNF005.name: steam-train carriage travel scene
SNF005.description: Wooden carriages, luggage racks, seats and moving windows form a steam train journey, with female passengers checking tickets at the window.
SNF005.design_tip: The sitting posture of the characters and the support of the seats are clear, and the luggage rack and the scenery outside the window jointly illustrate the travel environment.

SNF006.name: film-noir rainy-alley scene
SNF006.description: The reflection of the wetland, brick walls, door lights and the street in the distance form a rain alley. A female investigator in a windbreaker is walking with an umbrella.
SNF006.design_tip: Use dark levels and rim lighting to keep the characters readable, and the moist environment should not engulf the action.

SNF007.name: western-town saloon scene
SNF007.description: A wooden bar, louvered doors, round tables and old-style chandeliers constitute a Western tavern, with an adult female shopkeeper wiping glasses at the bar.
SNF007.design_tip: The characters, bar and guest seats are clearly layered, presenting a type of film and television environment based on daily business activities.

SNF008.name: detective-office investigation scene
SNF008.description: Desks, blinds, information cabinets and clue boards form a detective office, and the female detective stands in front of the board to sort out information.
SNF008.design_tip: Clue boards, lamps, and characters form narrative focal points, while paper information uses undecipherable schematic graphics.

SNG001.name: magic-academy classroom scene
SNG001.description: Arched windows, magic bookshelves, desks and floating lights form a magic academy classroom. Girls of middle school age wear full academy uniforms and practice controlling light balls at the table.
SNG001.design_tip: The magic light source illuminates the characters and surrounding objects, and the actions, props and academy space jointly express fantasy learning activities.

SNG002.name: adventurers-guild quest scene
SNG002.description: The mission board, reception desk, long table and travel equipment constitute the Adventurer's Guild, and the adult female ranger checks the mission notice.
SNG002.design_tip: The contact relationship between the characters, task boards and backpacks is clear, and the background furnishings reflect the public organizational space.

SNG003.name: fantasy-castle audience-hall scene
SNG003.description: Vaults, flags, stone steps and high windows form an elevated castle hall, where adult female lords receive visitors.
SNG003.design_tip: The height difference between the characters and the castle, the window light and the flag form a clear scale, and the emblem uses original graphics.

SNG004.name: alchemy-workshop research scene
SNG004.description: Curved tube instruments, books, material cabinets and luminous containers constitute an alchemy workshop, and an adult female alchemist observes magical reactions in front of the workbench.
SNG004.design_tip: Instruments are in contact with hands, and light effects serve the relationship between the workbench and characters; no realistic experimental steps are provided.

SNG005.name: elven-forest patrol scene
SNG005.description: Giant trees, forest trails, tree houses and luminous plants form the Elf Forest, with adult Elf women taking care of the plants along the trails.
SNG005.design_tip: Figures, trees and treehouses have understandable proportions, and footsteps have clear contact with the natural ground.

SNG006.name: dragon-ruins exploration scene
SNG006.description: Broken pillars, stone doors, moss and a sleeping dragon in the distance constitute ancient ruins. An adult female adventurer holds up a lamp to observe the entrance.
SNG006.design_tip: The dragon serves as a reference for the scale of the distant landscape, keeping the characters clear in the foreground and establishing an exploratory relationship with the entrance to the ruins.

SNG007.name: underwater-mermaid-city scene
SNG007.description: Coral arches, underwater streets, shell buildings and light beams form an underwater city, with adult mermaid women walking through it.
SNG007.design_tip: The figure has a complete fish tail and a clear proportion to the building, and the floating direction in the water, hair and light beams are consistent.

SNG008.name: crystal-temple ceremony scene
SNG008.description: Crystal pillars, stairs, light pools and altars constitute the temple. The adult priestess stands in front of the altar holding luminous objects in her hands.
SNG008.design_tip: The front-to-back relationship between the figure and the altar, the placement of the clothes and the direction of light are consistent, and the symbols are original fantasy decorations.

SNS001.name: space-station maintenance scene
SNS001.design_tip: The scale of characters and cabins is clear, the connections between cables and panels are clear, and the planet window view illustrates the environment.
SNS001.description: Portholes, circular bulkheads, work panels and equipment cabinets form a space station where an adult female engineer checks an interior panel.

SNS002.name: starship-bridge duty scene
SNS002.description: The curved console, driver's seat, star map and portholes form the starship cockpit, with an adult female captain commanding in front of the console.
SNS002.design_tip: The perspective of the console and the seat are consistent, the screen lighting matches the position of the characters, and the graphics are original interfaces.

SNS003.name: cyberpunk-city courier scene
SNS003.design_tip: Characters, delivery packages and streets have real contact, and neon light effects retain outlines and environmental layers.
SNS003.description: Elevated walkways, electronic screens, awnings and reflected neon form a futuristic street where an adult female courier crosses an intersection with a bag.

SNS004.name: mecha-hangar servicing scene
SNS004.description: A large mecha, maintenance racks, hoisting equipment and tool tables form a hangar, and an adult female mechanic inspects parts next to the legs of the mecha.
SNS004.design_tip: Create scenes with the scale difference between characters and giant equipment, and maintain believable connections between handheld tools and parts.

SNS005.name: underwater-research-station scene
SNS005.design_tip: The window is clearly separated from the underwater exterior, and the character's position and reflection are consistent with the lighting in the cabin.
SNS005.description: Transparent observation windows, laboratory benches, equipment compartments and fish outside form a deep-sea base where an adult female researcher observes marine life.

SNS006.name: wasteland-supply-outpost scene
SNS006.description: Repaired shacks, water storage tanks, shelves and dusty roads form a wasteland supply station, and adult female vendors organize water bottles and supplies.
SNS006.design_tip: Character activities and practical furnishings are used to illustrate the purpose of supplies, and the picture does not rely on specific game logos.

SNS007.name: shelter-supply-management scene
SNS007.description: Reinforced doors, storage racks, beds and ventilation ducts form an underground shelter, and adult female administrators hand out supply packages to residents.
SNS007.design_tip: The distribution area in the foreground is separated from the living area in the background. The characters and material packages are in real contact, maintaining a sense of daily life.

SNS008.name: alien-colony greenhouse scene
SNS008.description: Dome greenhouses, plant troughs, habitat pods and alien landscapes form a colony, and an adult female botanist inspects the planting area.
SNS008.design_tip: Keep people, cultivation tanks and domes at a reasonable scale, with terrain and sky establishing a fictional planet.

SNU001.name: school-gate arrival scene
SNU001.description: The teaching building, school gate, gate post and pedestrian entrance constitute the middle school campus. A high school girl in school uniform walks into the school with a backpack.
SNU001.design_tip: The school gate, school roads and teaching buildings are used to establish a hierarchy, and the characters and entrances maintain a believable proportion.

SNU002.name: campus tree-lined walkway scene
SNU002.description: Campus walks, tree shades, benches and teaching buildings constitute a middle school campus. Two junior high school girls in school uniforms communicate while walking.
SNU002.design_tip: The double steps and schoolbags are consistent with the perspective of the road, and the trees and teaching buildings illustrate the campus context.

SNU003.name: classroom break-time scene
SNU003.design_tip: Keep the desk arrangement and classmates' activities, which are different from teacher's teaching or study reading.
SNU003.description: Desks, a blackboard, windows and a teaching platform form a secondary-school classroom where a junior-high girl puts textbooks into her bag during a break.

SNU004.name: examination-room invigilation scene
SNU004.design_tip: The seats and aisles of the invigilators and candidates are clear, and the test papers and lists do not present real personal information.
SNU004.description: Spaced desks, a wall clock and a teaching platform form a secondary-school exam room where an adult female teacher patrols with a list while junior- and senior-high students answer quietly.

SNU005.name: academic-building corridor scene
SNU005.description: The classroom door, bulletin board and window railings form the corridor of the teaching building. Two high school girls in school uniforms exchange course materials after class.
SNU005.design_tip: Doorplate positions, corridor depth and handling materials convey school communication without relying on readable text.

SNU006.name: campus club-room activity scene
SNU006.description: Activity tables, storage cabinets, poster boards and handicrafts formed a club classroom, and junior high school girls and classmates made decorations for campus activities.
SNU006.design_tip: Handmade materials are in real contact with hands, and public activity tables and work displays illustrate the community space.

SNU007.name: art-classroom drawing scene
SNU007.description: Easels, still life tables, paints and large windows form a middle school art classroom, where high school girls practice sketching in front of still lifes.
SNU007.design_tip: Easels and brushes correspond to the figures' sightlines, and still life tables and other easels provide a teaching environment.

SNU008.name: music-classroom piano-practice scene
